newsitem.title: INDIA: Proton mulls three sites for India plant.
newsitem.headline: Proton mulls three sites for India plant.

text.p: Malaysia's Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) said it shortlisted three locations for its proposed car plant in India.
Proton's senior manager, corporate planning, Masahara Iwatu, was quoted by the Press Trust of India (PTI) as saying the company was looking at Chandigarh, Vishakapatnam and Madras.
Chandigarh lies roughly 250 kilometres north of New Delhi, while Madras and Vishakapatnam are in the southern states of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

Iwatu was quoted as saying Proton would initially form a fully-pwned subsidiary for the project with the possibility having an Indian partner later. He said he would make a final recommendation to the Proton board in three months and the groundwork for forming the company would start soon.

He told PTI the Indian car market did not have sufficient variety and there was immense scope for expansion. The news agency quoted Iwatu as saying Proton made 220,000 cars a year and sold them for an average of $ 24,000.
Malaysia's cabinet approved Proton's India project in May this year.
